newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb found at Russian arms firm.
newsitem.headline: Bomb found at Russian arms firm.

text.p: Russia's biggest arms exporter, speaking after police found a powerful mine in its Moscow headquarters, on Wednesday linked the discovery of the explosive device to what it called a smear campaign.

A statement from state-owned exporter Rosvooruzheniye said the planting of the mine coincided with "a frenzied campaign in some mass media aimed at discrediting Rosvooruzheniye and its leadership who are being accused of all thinkable and unthinkable sins".
The mine was found during night checks by guards in a passage leading to the office of company president Alexander Kotyolkin, the company said.

The statement said there had been several attempts on the life of Kotyolkin since he took over in 1994. Other officials had been threatened after cutting off "a number of semi-criminal structures" from the arms trade.

Police investigating the discovery of the two kg (four pound) "frog mine" declined to comment on the statement. The device is called a frog mine because it jumps into the air before exploding at a height of about 1.5 metres (four feet).

The International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) said on Wednesday Russia's arms exports almost doubled in 1995 to $3 billion, but sales were a far cry from the heady days of 1987 when the Soviet Union sold $29.1 billion worth of weapons.
Rosvooruzheniye holds a near monopoly in arms exports.
